name: Bloom Edition
tagline: A loud long-form magazine that never goes to print: every live event blooms into a star.
summary: Albretsen AS presented as a continuous edition of a dense, joyful magazine: ultra-wide display type, a literary serif, drop caps and marginalia on warm earth paper, with one cobalt for what is happening now. The hero's cover plate is a living constellation where each product grows as a sunflower spiral, one real event at a time. It reads as a body of work with range and output, and it holds all that density together with strict editorial control.
voice: Confident and declarative, short sentences that state facts and stop. Example: "Eleven entries. Two live, one building, one paused, seven retired. Nothing is taken down to look tidier."
motion: Slow cinematic fades and blooms, all of them pure CSS: nothing moves faster than its fact arrived, and nothing loops for show.
sound: A two-second sonic logo, 'Bloom' (a rising filtered breath that opens into three FM bell tones and a held fifth), plays when sound is switched on. After that, each product sounds one soft bell per event.
mark: The Seed: an abstract teardrop in flight with a cobalt satellite. It is a particle with velocity and the first star of a constellation, and it works from 16 px to poster size.

name: Continue.
tagline: A title screen at first light: one dot, two colours, one size, products that talk.
summary: The homepage is a game's title screen just before dawn: one viewport, a HUD frame, a menu of every product ever shipped, and a party chat where the live products report in. Everything is set in two colours and one type size, so the only loud thing is the name, and the full stop after it, which beats once for every real event. It reads as someone who has been playing for a long time and is still pressing Continue.
voice: Poetic and minimal; few words, each one load-bearing. "Most of it is awake before he is."
motion: Nothing moves on a timer: menu items are written in and erased by the scroll itself, the dawn dot rises with the menu's scroll timeline, and new messages slide in only when something real happens.
sound: Opt-in: each product sings one note of an A major pentatonic (MCP Emails A4, Toolrails C#5, Fun Libs E5, the site A5) through a single fading echo, so the feed becomes a slow chord.
mark: A single dot: the full stop after the name, also the menu cursor, the status light and the rising sun.

name: Gravity Issue
tagline: A sideways magazine printed in two inks, where every real event lands on the cover.
summary: albretsen.no reads like the current issue of a bright, curious magazine: a cover story, a contents spread and a colophon, turned sideways and printed in just Sol orange and Umber. The products are the articles and the live feed is the cover photo, made of real events falling onto a timeline. Everything is type and CSS, which quietly shows the craft without having to say so.
type: Bricolage Grotesque 600 / wdth 100, 11px caps (labels; no mono)
voice: Playful, curious and forward-looking, written like a good magazine standfirst: "Every product here began as a question: would anyone want this?"
motion: Events land on the strip with real gravity: they fall, bounce twice and settle, while a slow halftone vector field drifts behind the cover and dents wherever something lands.
sound: No sound on the page; the sonic logo is a rising major sixth on two soft sine voices followed by a low felt thump, an idea landing.
mark: Four bars, one per product (MCP Emails, Fun Libs, Toolrails, albretsen.no), whose heights are each product's share of the last twelve live events, so the logo and favicon are redrawn by the data.

name: Carrier
tagline: A 1990s personal homepage rebuilt as tomorrow's interface: one pixel face, one hue, one character grid.
summary: Carrier takes the honest bits of the 90s homepage (the marquee, the hit counter, the directory listing, the guestbook) and rebuilds them on a strict monospace grid where type only scales in whole pixels. Everything is VT323 on shades of a single rose hue, so the precision does the showing off. It suits Albretsen AS because the page behaves like the work: small, exact, fast, and a bit funny about itself.
type: VT323 at 25px, 1 font pixel = 1 screen pixel (text)
voice: Warm, dry and exact, like a friend who reads changelogs for fun: "The tape only moves when something happens."
motion: Nothing moves unless it is answering you or reporting a real event: hovers invert a cell, presses fill it, and the tape steps left one whole character at a time.
sound: Opt-in square-wave notes on the A major pentatonic, one per product (MCP Emails A4, Toolrails C#5, Fun Libs E5, albretsen.no A3), played as real events arrive.
mark: A:\>_ : the DOS prompt for drive A, read as Albretsen, with a cursor that fills on hover; the favicon is the same prompt drawn on a 16-pixel grid.

name: Stille
tagline: A quiet terminal that keeps score: every product playing in one six-minute piano roll.
summary: Stille (Norwegian for still, quiet) treats albretsen.no as a terminal pane drawn on a visible, asymmetric grid. The live feed is set as a score in box-drawing characters, one lane per kind of event, so the mix of products reads as music and the rests read as honest silence. Light and dark trade places at every section, the wordmark slows letter by letter into space, and the visitor has a lane of their own.
voice: Poetic and minimal, plain Norwegian understatement, never selling. Example: "I build software, quietly, and keep what earns its place."
motion: Nothing moves by itself; only hover, focus and press answer the hand, and the score redraws one column at a time like a terminal.
sound: Off until asked; turning it on plays three bells stacked in fifths, a rest, then one low D, and afterwards each event rings a soft pentatonic note for its lane.
mark: A pure wordmark, ALBRETSEN in condensed light capitals, with tracking that widens letter by letter (0 to 0.23 em) so the name slows into silence.

name: Current
tagline: The name, drawn only by lines that shift half a step. Live events pass through it as pulses.
summary: A field of warm umber lines after Bridget Riley's Current. The name fills the first screen, and the only thing that draws it is lines shifting phase. The cursor works as a lens and every real event from the products sends one pulse through the field. It reads as control, not decoration: one rule, applied exactly, which suits a company that ships quietly and keeps only what works.
voice: Dry understatement. States the fact and stops. Example: "Builds software. Keeps what pays for itself."
motion: Nothing moves on its own: the field bends under the cursor like a lens and sends one pulse per real event, and it stays still under reduced motion.
sound: Opt-in Web Audio: each product has its own note in D major pentatonic (MCP Emails D4, Toolrails E4, Fun Libs A4, the site B4), struck once per event.
mark: A monogram A drawn by the field's rule: inside the letter, the stripes shift half a period and thicken. Nothing outlines it.

name: Blue Hour
tagline: A festival bill set as a quiet document, in nine depths of one blue.
summary: The products are billed like acts on a festival poster: live ones as headliners, building and paused below, retired ones in small print and still on the bill. The page is laid out like a document with wide margins, where the numbers sit in the margin and the products talk to each other in a group chat. It works through absence: one hue, one rounded typeface, no lines, and the size of the type sets the order.
voice: Numbers first, adjectives never. "2 live. 1 building. 1 paused. 7 retired. Since 2016, software built to pay for itself."
motion: Kinetic weight: type blooms from hairline to black as it arrives, and words in the chat come out of a blur, all on transforms and font weight with no layout shift.
sound: An opt-in generative ambient drone in D that opens its filter as activity rises, with one soft pentatonic note per real event, pitched by product.
mark: A lowercase Nunito 800 wordmark, 'albretsen', with spacing set by hand per letter (tight at 'al', opening through 'bret', even to the end), so it reads like the top line of a poster.

name: Threshold
tagline: The page is a heat grid of product by minute; the name is set on top of the silence.
summary: Every product writes into one full-bleed grid: four bands, one column per minute, lit in a single electric cyan when someone uses something Asgeir built. Three typefaces that clash on purpose (a wide grotesk, a condensed italic serif and a mono) sit on that grid with New Wave nerve and Swiss discipline underneath. Quiet minutes are drawn as honestly as busy ones, so the page shows real use without having to say so.
voice: Poetic and minimal: short, exact, a little amused by itself. "Each square is a minute. Each light, someone."
motion: Nothing moves unless something real happens or the cursor asks: a cell flashes when an event lands, the name gains weight near the pointer, and the theme crosses the page one column at a time.
sound: Opt-in Web Audio: a soft sine note per product on each live event (a pentatonic per row), a dry tick when the cursor crosses a cell, and a falling sweep of ticks as the theme crosses the page.
mark: Four right-aligned bars against a vertical 'now' line, their lengths taken from the last fifteen minutes of each product, so the logo (and the favicon) changes shape with the data.

name: Afterimage
tagline: A letter set on a pixel grid, with the software's activity in orbit around the name.
summary: Afterimage treats Albretsen AS like a piece of creative code: one narrow column, everything set on a pixel grid, and the only thing that moves is the real activity of the products, landing on concentric rings around his name. It borrows Vera Molnár's habit of building a strict system and then breaking it by one pixel. The work is the evidence; nothing on the page has to brag.
voice: Playful and curious, says little, leaves things for you to find. "I build software, then watch what it does."
motion: Completely still, except the feed: when something real happens, every event steps one slot outward along its ring in six hard frames.
sound: Opt-in square-wave blips through a short echo, tuned to A major pentatonic, one note per product.
mark: An A drawn twice on a 9x9 grid, the inner stroke an echo of the outer, with the top-right pixel left out on purpose.

name: Pust
tagline: A front page set in a terminal: two greens, one monospace grid, events orbiting the name.
summary: Pust (Norwegian for breath) treats albretsen.no like a serious publication printed on a phosphor screen. The name is set huge, cropped and overlapped like a masthead cut from type, while real events from every product drift around it in a slow orbit. Two colours and monospace only: the restraint shows the taste, and the live orbit shows the output.
voice: Norwegian plainness: short, declarative, a little dry, with a Norwegian word where it is the plainer one. "Apps, SaaS and infrastructure for AI agents. Built in Norway, kept if it pays for itself."
motion: Everything moves in CSS at the pace of breathing: a 7-minute orbit, typing in steps, a collage that leans toward the cursor, nothing driven by JavaScript.
sound: Opt-in soft key clicks synthesized from filtered noise, one per character as each new event types itself in.
mark: a░: a bold lowercase a followed by a light-shade block, the cursor waiting for the next breath.

name: Low Sun
tagline: A vermilion broadsheet whose masthead casts the real shadow of the sun over Oslo.
summary: The page is the colour of the Nordic sun sitting on the horizon, and the name Albretsen fills the first screen like a masthead, casting a long shadow computed from the actual sun over Oslo. Below it every product plays on a live musical score, and the masthead's variable weight thickens when the products are busy. It reads like a serious publication with a sense of humour: proof of taste, delivered as telemetry.
voice: Warm, witty and exact, like a good newspaper column. Example: "Busier days get bolder type; quiet ones get a lighter touch."
motion: Nothing moves unless something happened: a real event pulses one letter and tears a thin slice of the masthead for a tenth of a second, then everything settles.
sound: An opt-in music box: each event plucks the pentatonic pitch of its row on the score, a deploy plays a soft chord, a glitch ticks.
mark: An abstract low sun: a disc above a horizon line with its long shadow below, reused as the status glyph (up, rising, on the horizon, set).

name: Afterimage
tagline: Op Art restraint: one silent half, one half under tension, and one blue line.
summary: The page is a field of black bands that begin dead straight and slowly bend, the way a Bridget Riley painting builds energy until it reaches maximum tension. The name sits half on silence and half inside the field, inverted by it. Albretsen AS should read as precise and quietly ambitious: the effect is technical, the luxury is in what has been left out.
voice: Confident and declarative. Short sentences that state facts and stop. Example: "Everything shipped, still running or retired. Nothing removed."
motion: A generative band field that starts straight, takes on tension over six seconds and then moves no faster than breathing; the feed is a constant-speed tape where empty stretches are real time passing.
sound: Opt-in Web Audio only: a struck sine per live event, pitched by product with a faint glassy partial, plus a dry tick when a product comes into focus.
mark: Seven parallel lines bent by a seeded wave, one of them blue; a new seed every visit, so no two visitors see the same mark, and the seed is printed in the footer.

name: Bloom Index
tagline: Paper, ink and one magenta signal: an Are.na-style index of everything built, with a live log typing beside it.
summary: The site is an index of blocks on a visible 12-column grid. Three typefaces that clash on purpose (a condensed italic serif, an expanded black grotesk and a mono) are held in line by that grid. Everything is paper and ink, and the single spot colour means one thing only: something is happening right now. That reads as clarity and taste for a builder whose products keep running while he works on the next one.
voice: Terse engineer. Short declaratives, units and dates, no adjectives that cannot be measured. "Builds software that pays for itself."
motion: Teletype: each new log line arrives one character every 18 ms behind a magenta caret, the mark blooms once per event, and nothing moves when nothing happens.
sound: Opt-in ambient drone in D that opens up as activity rises, and each real event blooms one pentatonic note voiced by its product.
mark: The Bloom Point: an ink disc overprinted by a magenta disc, with the overlap left as a darker lens. It is drawn only with CSS and swells briefly on each live event.

name: Bitspark
tagline: A 1-bit desktop where every product sings its own note.
summary: Albretsen AS as a bright System 7 desktop: black ink, white paper, one hot crimson spark, a grid you can see. One live event fills the window at a time in an ultra-wide face, while a four-lane chorus shows the rhythm of every product at once. It reads as optimistic, exact and fast, someone who ships and keeps shipping.
voice: Terse engineer, upbeat. States what shipped and what it does, never sells. Example: "Ships software that pays for itself."
motion: Still by default; each real event gets one 360 ms pass of sliced, offset, dithered glitch, then holds dead still.
sound: Opt-in square-wave beeps: MCP Emails C5, Fun Libs E5, Toolrails G5, albretsen.no C6, so the feed plays a C-major chorus at the speed of real traffic.
mark: A 16x16 pixel A with a five-pixel crimson spark at its shoulder, drawn for the favicon first and only ever scaled by whole pixels.

name: Surface Tension
tagline: Every product is a surface; every real event lands on it as a chrome drop.
summary: A dark, single-hue (OKLCH 180) world of wet chrome and translucent gel, Y2K futurism with the volume turned down. The hero is a full-bleed, real-time strip of the last fifteen minutes across MCP Emails, Fun Libs, Toolrails and the site itself, and the name above it is set in a variable font whose width is literally the traffic of the last five minutes. It reads as one person running several working systems at once, and shows it instead of saying it.
voice: Terse engineer with an indie grin: short declaratives, numbers over adjectives, one dry joke per screen. "Shipped. Including the dead ones."
motion: Time moves at the speed of the clock and nothing else; drops fall and ripple on arrival, type tightens as you scroll away, all of it driven by CSS scroll timelines and real events.
sound: Off by default; switching it on plays 'the drop', a synthesized sine that breaks the surface and rings into a glassy fifth, then each event lands as a near-silent pentatonic drip per product.
mark: The Drop: a chrome-and-gel blob shaped by three low harmonics from a random 24-bit seed, so every visit gets a different, always-recognisable drop (and favicon).

name: Full Stop
tagline: Ink, paper and one dot that takes the colour of whatever just happened.
summary: A New Wave page in the Weingart and Greiman line: stretched-wide type, stepped lines, the grid drawn on the paper, every scale labelled. The page has no colour of its own. Colour arrives only when a product does something, so the live feed is drawn as a piano roll, and the logo, a single dot, always shows the hue of the latest event. Retired work stays on the timeline beside the live products, because a record with 7 retired entries and 2 live ones is more convincing than any adjective.
voice: Numbers first, adjectives never; every claim is a count, a year or a unit. "Shipping software since 2016: 11 products, 2 live, 1 building, 1 paused, 7 retired."
motion: Teletype: text arrives one character at a time behind a cursor in the live colour, and notes drift left at the speed of the wall clock.
sound: Off until asked; then each typed character is a 28 ms band-passed noise click synthesized in Web Audio, with a lower thud for spaces.
mark: A single full stop, a filled circle whose colour is the hue of the most recent event (the favicon follows it too).

name: Albedo
tagline: A pale instrument that reports what happened, and very little else.
summary: Albretsen AS presented the way a lab presents its findings: a high-key, nearly white page where the only thing that moves is real activity, arriving as pixel dots on a world map and as lines of type. Lots of air, very small type and one condensed name. Asgeir comes across as someone who measures before he speaks, and the evidence is live.
voice: Dry understatement in the register of a methods section: it states the observation and leaves the reader to be impressed. Example: "Positions approximate to country or city. Quiet periods are real."
motion: Text arrives character by character like a teletype, a new dot gets one square ring of signal, and nothing else moves unless something actually happened.
sound: Silent page. The sonic logo, written up in BRAND.md, is a 228 Hz sine with a short return ping two octaves up, like a sensor registering an echo.
mark: An 8 by 8 pixel A drawn for 16 px first, with one detached pixel in the top-right corner as the signal; on the site that pixel changes colour when the site deploys.

name: Preprint
tagline: The company as a working paper: greys, margins and figures, with colour only when something happens.
summary: Albretsen AS presented the way a careful researcher presents results: one narrow column, sidenotes in the margin, a live figure and a table of every product, retired ones included. The page is greyscale; colour belongs to live events and fades to grey with a 120-second half-life, so you can read how recent an event is from its colour. The tone is calm because the numbers carry the argument.
voice: Numbers first, adjectives never; short declaratives a referee could check. Example: "113,000+ installs, $782 MRR, 2 products live, 1 building."
motion: Every card is a damped spring (stiffness 210, damping 22): new events drop onto the stack, the rest are pushed down and keep some of that momentum, and a sideways pull lets the stack flow and settle back with inertia.
sound: Opt-in sonification of the feed: each product has its own sine note from D major pentatonic (Fun Libs A4, MCP Emails B4, Toolrails E5, the site D4), with a few milliseconds of synthesized grain on the attack.
mark: A 7 x 7 field of short strokes, like grain under a lens: the base flow is fixed, and each visit adds a seeded perturbation, printed in a sidenote, so the mark is slightly different every time.

name: One Spot
tagline: A printed document with one ink, one paper and one spot of signal green.
summary: The site reads like a Dutch exhibition catalogue: a strict three-column page with wide margins, a single serif family, and marginalia doing the quiet work. One spot colour at hue 120 marks only what is happening now (the newest event on a dot-grid world, the live products, the thing under your cursor), so the eye learns that green-yellow means signal. Saying little and showing density suits a builder whose work speaks through live numbers and a long, honest list of what he has made.
voice: Few words, curious and a little playful, never selling. "Players have countries. Agents don't, so they live on the bottom line."
motion: Nothing moves unless you touch it: hover, focus and press get small, exact responses, and the page itself stays still.
sound: Opt-in soft key clicks, synthesised in Web Audio, as each new event types itself into the margin.
mark: The Field: 25 dots on a 5x5 grid whose sizes follow a random point of density, with the densest dot in spot colour, drawn fresh and numbered for every visit.

name: Brev
tagline: A letter written in a code editor, signed by a constellation of live data.
summary: Brev (Norwegian for letter) presents Asgeir as a person writing to you: one narrow column of warm serif text with editor line numbers in the gutter, set on a strict character grid. In the middle of the letter, a night editor pane holds a constellation in which every real product event is a star that drifts out along its product's vector as it ages. Plain words, a lot of craft, and proof that the work is running right now.
type: Newsreader Caption (no monospace, the grid does that job)
voice: Norwegian plainness: short, true sentences, warm without being sweet, with a Norwegian word where it fits. Example: "I build software in Norway, and I keep what pays for itself."
motion: Motion comes from the scroll and from real time only: rows type in by four character cells as they enter view, the sky dims as you leave it, and stars move one cell at a time because they really did get older.
sound: Opt-in ambient drone (A and E) whose filter opens with activity, a fourth voice above the threshold of eight events a minute, and one soft bell per event from that product's own little scale.
mark: Four stars, the newest event from each product, joined into a figure; the logo is literally the current shape of the data, with a fixed snapshot used for the favicon.

name: Dot Plot
tagline: A data-journalism graphic about one company, set entirely in monospace, with a full stop for a logo.
summary: Albretsen AS presented the way The Pudding or the FT graphics desk would present a dataset: paper, ink, one spot colour, annotations and an honest chart of every product including the retired ones. The live feed is the lead story, one event at a time and very large, and every sentence on the page ends in the brand mark. It reads as someone who measures things, ships things, and finds the whole business quietly funny.
voice: Dry understatement, written like a chart annotation: short, exact, slightly amused. "Builds software in Norway. Some of it is running right now."
motion: A dot-grid sheet drifts behind the page; each real event drops a spot dot that echoes outward in rings, nudges the grid as they pass, then drifts and fades over ten minutes.
sound: Opt-in Web Audio: the sonic logo is one clean dot of a note followed by four echoes that drift slightly flat and darker, then a low full stop.
mark: A full stop in the spot colour: it is the logo, the favicon, and the last character of every headline and every live event.

name: Hjemmeside
tagline: A 1996 personal homepage, rebuilt by someone with 2026 taste.
summary: The site is a hjemmeside: a fixed index frame, a plain page, underlined blue links and a log of what is happening right now, built with care and no decoration. The products and the live log do the talking, which suits a person who ships quietly and keeps the honest record, retired experiments included.
voice: Plain, light and unhurried, with a Norwegian word where a Norwegian would use one. 'Hei. Every product, as it happens. Nothing is replayed or sped up.'
motion: Everything that moves is a damped spring that keeps its velocity, so a burst of events pushes the log down with real inertia, and quiet hours stay still.
sound: Off until asked; then a soft synthesised sine tick per event, pitched per product, plus a two-note chime for the toggle.
mark: An 8 by 8 pixel capital A with one blue pixel beside it, drawn for the 16 px favicon first; the blue pixel is the pulse and springs each time an event arrives.

name: Exhale
tagline: The name takes the shape of your screen; the page breathes from paper to ink as you scroll.
summary: Web brutalism with a warm pulse: a stretched editorial serif name that fills the first viewport exactly, then a page that inhales (paper) and exhales (ink) section by section, with one live event at a time set huge. The cursor is the underscore from the a_ mark, a person mid-sentence, which stretches with velocity and breathes when still. It reads as one person who ships, counts and keeps the record honest.
voice: Numbers first, adjectives never; warm because it is plain and first-person. Example: "10 years of building software that pays for itself."
motion: Slow cinematic fades from blur, 1.4 to 2.4 seconds, and a whole-page colour inversion that crossfades as each section crosses the middle of the screen.
sound: Silent page; the sonic logo is two breaths, a filtered-noise inhale and a sine exhale on a falling fourth, 1.8 seconds in total.
mark: a_ : a lowercase serif a followed by a typing underscore in amber; the underscore is also the site's cursor.

name: Daylight Lattice
tagline: A title card in daylight: one grotesk at cinema scale over a living lattice of minutes.
summary: Albretsen AS is shown as a lattice of products and minutes, with each square lit by real activity. The name is set like the opening title of a film, in warm daylight and pastel mint, so the ambition reads as big while the tone stays calm and generous. The mark is an A made from the busiest cells of that lattice, so the logo and the live data share one language.
voice: Warm and witty, with no swagger: it states facts and then smiles. Example: "Four in play. Seven retired with honours."
motion: Everything moves on damped springs: cells pop when an event lands, the lattice glides one minute left with inertia, and links lean in and settle.
sound: Off until asked. Switching it on plays "A in daylight", an A-major arpeggio strummed upward that lands on the octave over a soft A bed, after which each event gives a quiet pitched tick.
mark: A 5x5 lattice in which the hottest cells spell the letter A. It doubles as the favicon, and each cell answers a different product live.

name: fullt hus
tagline: a full-house data front page where the live feed sets every colour, weight and width
summary: albretsen.no as one dense, joyful data-journalism front page that fits a single screen: the name is a live chart, a ticker tape runs every real event, and each product owns a hue that only appears when the feed puts it there. it shows range and output at a glance and sounds plain about it, the way a norwegian would.
voice: lowercase, plain, a little dry, with a norwegian word where it fits. 'stille · nothing for 20 s'
motion: kinetic type driven by data: each event ripples weight through the name, and the font trades weight for width so the layout never moves.
sound: no sound on the page; the sonic logo is four plucked notes, one per product hue, landing on a held fifth.
mark: a single-storey lowercase a: the bowl is an orbit with a moon in its aperture, and the stem is a stacked bar of the live product mix.

name: Widescreen
tagline: A name drawn in pixels on a Crouwel lattice, two screens wide, run sideways like film.
summary: Albretsen is set as a 55 by 7 pixel wordmark on a visible grid, and the grid's unit is the wordmark's own pixel, so every panel and column lands on the same lattice. The page scrolls sideways through three frames: the name and a live stack of real events, the products as a run of poster columns, and the address. It is near-black and still. The only things that move are the feed cards, and the only colour is one electric violet spark.
voice: Short, flat, declarative. States what exists and stops. Example: "Eleven products. Four in motion. Seven retired, kept in view."
motion: The page itself never moves; only new feed cards drop onto the stack, and with reduced motion they appear without transition.
sound: Opt-in generative ambience: a low D drone that opens up as real activity rises, with each event striking one note of a D pentatonic lattice in a register owned by its product.
mark: A favicon-first pixel A on a 16 px grid with one violet spark pixel at its upper right; the same spark ends the 55 by 7 wordmark.

name: Full Stop
tagline: One violet field, one Garamond voice, and a full stop for every thing that happens.
summary: Albretsen AS as a quiet operator: a page that is completely still except for the work itself. Every real event from every product lands as one full stop in a constellation drawn without lines, set in classical book typography on a fully saturated violet. The tone is calm and literary, like a modern AI lab. The effect is someone who finishes things and does not need to say so.
type: EB Garamond with true small caps and old-style figures (text)
None: commands are set in the book face, lining figures
voice: Terse engineer. Short declaratives that end in a period, facts before adjectives. "I build software, ship it, and keep what pays."
motion: Nothing moves except the feed: a new full stop fades in over 900 ms (or appears instantly with reduced motion), and the page itself never animates.
sound: Silent on the page. The sonic logo, described in BRAND.md, is a single soft felt-piano note with a sung fifth above it: a full stop you can hear.
mark: The EB Garamond full stop, drawn from the font's own outline: cream on violet, used tiny after the name and enormous as cropped image.

name: Colophon
tagline: A Swiss grid set in book type, where the only colour on the page is something happening right now.
summary: Colophon treats albretsen.no like the last page of a well-made book: the note that says exactly how the thing was made. Twelve visible columns, Garamond with true small capitals and old-style figures, and a monospace log; everything is grey until an event arrives, and then, briefly, it is green. It reads as rigorous, quiet and quietly busy, which is what a company that ships many products alone should look like.
voice: Confident, declarative, understated; states and stops. Example: "Keeps what earns its place, retires what doesn't."
motion: Kinetic typography driven only by real events: the current sentence types itself, the newest log line types in, the name ripples once, and the orbit mark turns once a minute because a minute passes.
sound: Opt-in soft keyboard clicks, synthesized with Web Audio from filtered noise, one per character as the sentence types.
mark: The Orbit: four concentric rings, one per product in the feed, with a grain for each recent event placed by its second within the minute, so the mark is the shape of the data and the favicon redraws itself.

name: room 24
tagline: a one-man exhibition on a red wall, labelled in pixels, lowercase, with the failures still hanging
summary: albretsen.no as a gallery room painted one saturated red (oklch hue 24): wall text for the hero, a stack of black object labels for the live feed, and the products hung as a permanent collection where the retired works stay on the wall. it fits albretsen as because it is self-made and a bit cheeky, and the work is shown, labelled and left to speak for itself.
voice: dry curatorial understatement, all lowercase, never selling: "the retired works stay on the wall. taking them down would be marketing."
motion: everything arrives like house lights coming up: 1.6–2.2 s fades, a wordmark whose pixels slowly settle from round to square, and feed labels sliding in behind each other at walking pace.
sound: opt-in only: soft synthesized keyboard clicks (filtered noise plus a low sine thock) as each new feed label types itself in, with a deeper click for spaces.
mark: a pure lowercase wordmark, 'albretsen', in bold bitcount, letter-spaced to the full width of its wall like an exhibition title, so the spacing is the room divided evenly.

name: Uncut
tagline: Opening titles for a company that shows the whole reel, outtakes included.
summary: Albretsen AS presented as the opening titles of a film that is still being shot: condensed capitals rising over a horizon, a raw tail -f of every product running underneath, and a cast list where retired experiments keep their credit. Everything is grey; colour only appears when something real happens while you are watching, so the page itself proves the work is alive.
voice: Playful, curious and unvarnished: says the quiet part, shows the failures, never sells. "I build software to find out what pays. Some of it does. The rest is listed below anyway."
motion: Titles rise over the horizon once; after that the only motion is a controlled glitch and a decoding line, each fired by a real event and never by a timer.
sound: Opt-in projector-room drone whose filter opens with real activity, with one pentatonic pluck per event through a dark tape delay.
mark: _/\_ : an ASCII peak standing on a horizon line, typed in mono; in the favicon the horizon lights up in the colour of the latest event.

name: Honest Deck
tagline: Every bet, face up: a self-dealing deck of candy cards under an airbrushed sunset.
summary: Every product Asgeir has shipped is a glossy card in a three.js deck that deals itself as you scroll, live ones face up with their real numbers and retired ones stamped FOLDED. Showing the losers next to the winners is the point: it reads as someone who places many bets, keeps score in public and has nothing to hide. The 80s chrome-and-airbrush look in a candy palette keeps it optimistic, technical and nothing like a finance firm.
voice: Brutally honest and short, numbers before adjectives, losses stated plainly: "Eleven products dealt so far: two pay, one is being built, one is paused, seven folded."
motion: Things move like cards in a dealer's hands: they leave a deck, flip face up mid-air and land on a spring, and the hero deal is 64 pre-rendered frames scrubbed by scroll.
sound: Off by default; when switched on, every deal, shuffle, shortcut and dropped card gives a short synthesised card snap, riffled for multi-card moves.
mark: A house-of-cards A, two leaning cards with a third lying across them edge-on, next to an 80s chrome ALBRETSEN wordmark outlined from Unbounded 800.

name: Night Shift Paper
tagline: A paper-cut desktop on a Norwegian night, where you can drag the sun up.
summary: The homepage is a desktop operating system cut from paper and lit by one sodium-orange sun. Windows are taped sheets you can drag, the dock holds the real product icons, and a raw WebGL shader draws torn hills, aurora and a sun that rises as you scroll or drag it. Everything looks hand-cut but is built in code. That gap carries the brand: a builder with taste who ships.
voice: Plain, warm and a little nocturnal, and always concrete about what shipped. Example: "Builds software that pays for itself. Cut from scratch after the day job and shipped before morning."
motion: Paper physics: sheets unfold, drop, lift and peel, and they swing against the direction you drag them, all on damped linear() springs.
sound: Off by default. Once it is on: synthesized paper rustles on drops and dialogs, a dry tick on the dock and tabs, and a soft two-note chime when you click the sun.
mark: A paper 'A' whose counter is a window onto a rising sodium sun under an aurora strip, stacked as seven real paper layers that fan apart in 3D.

name: Uranographia
tagline: A star atlas of working software: every product is a constellation drawn from its own number.
summary: The site is a 19th-century star atlas rendered with modern data craft. MCP Emails is 17 stars for 17 tools, Fun Libs carries 113 cluster stars for 113,000 installs, Toolrails has 4 bright feeders for 4 connectors and Harbor holds 549 grains of dust for 549 commits; retired products stay on the rim as constellationes obsoletae. Every live event from the products falls into its constellation as a meteor, so the sky visibly grows while you read and says 'prolific and exact' without claiming it.
voice: Calm, exact, catalogue-like; the numbers carry the boast. Example: "Seventeen stars for seventeen tools."
motion: Everything moves the way the sky does: gravity for arrivals, slow precession for transitions, and the pointer as a mass that stars lean toward, all on the Web Animations API.
sound: Off until asked; then each live event that lands in a constellation rings one soft sine bell, pitched per product.
mark: The asterism A: an A drawn as a constellation with gapped atlas lines, a diffraction sparkle at the apex and the crossbar running on as a dotted vector.

name: Tension Prism
tagline: The name is the prism: a glass lattice that every live event passes through as light.
summary: Albretsen AS as a crystal held under tension. The ALBRETSEN wordmark is grown from about 1,900 live SVG facets that bend under the pointer, shatter on click and re-crystallise into each product's name, while every real event from his products enters as a white photon and leaves as one mint beam. It reads as hard to build and still perfectly held together, which is the case for the person behind it.
voice: Short, declarative, measured in facts rather than adjectives. Example: "White light in, one colour out."
motion: Everything is under tension: things stretch toward where they are going, overshoot slightly and snap back into the lattice.
sound: Opt-in glass tones: each live event rings a short bell-like partial, pitched per product, and a shatter rings an octave lower.
mark: The Prism A, a five-row lattice of glass triangles with the counter knocked out, mint at the apex and the two exit facets like a ray passing through a prism.

name: Kiln Light
tagline: A quiet sunlit room, one day of light, and the products fired as glazed tiles.
summary: Albretsen AS is a small sunlit room built from three.js primitives, with each real product logo fired as a ceramic tile. Scrolling scrubs 64 pre-rendered frames: the camera walks in while one day passes, and further down the same room runs live so the visitor can turn it over. The calm and the honest materials let the technical depth speak without decoration, which suits one developer who ships, keeps what earns and archives the rest.
voice: Plain, unhurried and exact, with one warm word per line. Example: "Quiet software that pays for itself."
motion: Only the light moves on its own. Everything else enters with a focus pull (blur to sharp, a 14 px rise, expo-out) and settles with at most 4% overshoot.
sound: Opt-in Web Audio synthesis tuned to A5: tok on a glazed tile, ting of glass, a glide in fifths, a clay thum, and embers crackling at dusk.
mark: An arch with a ledge reads as a soft A, and a single glaze-blue sphere rests on the ledge. It is the room's window and the one drop of glaze that every icon carries.

name: Infrared Fable
tagline: A real landscape photographed in light you can't see, with a storybook living inside it.
summary: Poly Haven photographs graded like Kodak Aerochrome infrared film, with the name set behind the treeline and a pointed-arch aperture that opens from the horizon into a second scene as you scroll. Hand-coloured public-domain plates (butterflies, ferns, Grandville's comet) and a spring-physics specimen deck make the products tangible. The craft is in the layering and physics; the copy stays dry and factual, which is how a company that keeps only what pays should sound.
voice: Storybook warmth with ledger-dry facts: short, concrete, no adjectives doing the work of numbers. "Whatever pays. If it earns its keep, it stays in the field."
motion: Things rise from behind the horizon, open through arches and settle on springs: depth first, then tension, then release.
sound: Off by default; once turned on, flipping a plate rings a soft three-partial chime pitched per product and sending a card away is a short paper swish.
mark: A pointed-arch window onto an infrared treeline at sunset, where the road to the horizon forms the counter of an A, beside a Gloock wordmark with a magenta Martian Mono AS tab.

name: Cloud Chamber
tagline: A calm rose lab where chrome letters fall, collide and leave particle tracks
summary: The hero is a working physics chamber: ALBRETSEN in liquid chrome drops onto a measured floor, can be grabbed and thrown, and every hard impact draws bubble-chamber spirals in canvas 2D. Live product events (MCP Emails, Fun Libs, Toolrails) enter as labelled tracks and are written to a detector log. It turns real activity into visible physics, which suits a builder whose work runs quietly in the background and is judged by what it leaves behind.
voice: Scientific calm: plain sentences, numbers set like measurements, nothing raised. "Shipped, measured, stopped. Each taught something the live ones use."
motion: Long, even easing with at most one overshoot; text decodes into place out of a churn of brand glyphs, and sections open along the logo's break line.
sound: Off until asked; then glassy two-partial pings, pitched by impact speed, and a soft low tick when a product event crosses the chamber.
mark: Unbounded's A cut along one slanted line with the upper shard shifted; the break line is reused as the section transition and the specimen's hover state.

name: Salon Refusé
tagline: A museum wall after hours where every frame is a program and a UV torch shows the maths underneath.
summary: The homepage is a jade gallery wall at night, made from three.js renders of a real CC0 gilt frame. The frame in the hero holds a live canvas-2D work that paints itself stroke by stroke. A UV torch follows the cursor and burns through the paint, the products and even the headline to show the underdrawing: vector fields, catenaries, construction grids, type specs. The products hang as real logos on museum mats, with a red 'sold' dot on the two that earn money. Retired products sit in a storeroom rack instead of being hidden. The craft is in the hidden layer, so visitors discover his taste themselves instead of being told about it.
voice: Dry, exact, slightly insolent: a gallery that breaks its own rules. 'Retired, not destroyed.'
motion: Light before movement. The lamps flicker on, works unveil top-down with a clip-path, frames swing as real damped pendulums, and the UV torch opens and closes on a WAAPI-animated @property.
sound: Off until asked. Then a synthesised light-switch click when the lamps come on or a work is rehung, and a soft glass tone when the UV torch lights up.
mark: A frame hung deliberately crooked (−7°) from a spark-green nail on a taut wire, with a four-point spark inside; the wordmark is Instrument Serif Italic with the nail dot on the A.

name: Cold Boot
tagline: The site boots like a machine and lands like light through glass.
summary: A short mono boot log lists the products and their numbers, then lifts away. A soft glow cracks into shards of prismatic light, and that still becomes live glass the visitor can push a lens through. Everything is warm grey; colour appears only where light is refracted (ray-traced caustics, the amber of a NASA night photograph, each product's own icon). It reads as an engineer with taste: precise, quiet, and clearly able to build the hard thing.
voice: Nordic understatement: short declaratives, numbers instead of adjectives, the machine allowed one dry joke. Example: "dmesg · the boot never really ends"
motion: Springs, not easing curves: everything settles like glass on a table, and anything that moves trails two fading echoes.
sound: Off by default; when switched on, each live event rings a quiet glass tick with two decaying echoes, pitched per product.
mark: An A built from two prism legs whose crossbar is a beam of light entering from outside the left leg, set beside a Schibsted Grotesk 560 wordmark and a mono AS.

name: Specimen Atlas
tagline: A natural-history atlas of things that were built, lit by the sun over Oslo.
summary: Albretsen AS is presented as a catalogue of specimens: each product is pinned to a cream card, photographed like an editorial still life and kept running. The hero is one beautiful render, a brass and glass radiolarian after Haeckel, built from three.js primitives, which comes alive in the hand and is re-lit by the real sun over Norway. It shows precision and taste without saying so, and every interaction (loupe, plate stack, drawer of tags) is hand-rolled spring physics.
voice: A curator with a sense of humour: exact labels, short sentences, one wry italic aside. Example: "The atlas: four specimens, under glass."
motion: Everything moves on hand-rolled springs that keep their momentum: things settle like a specimen laid on a tray, and nothing animates from zero.
sound: Off until asked; then synthesised paper (filtered noise) for plates and tags, and a small brass bell when the specimen comes alive.
mark: A lattice A: five nodes joined like a molecule or a small network graph, apex stained eosin; set beside Albretsen in outlined Fraunces 600.

name: Key Frame
tagline: A one-person animation studio for software: cel-shaded, duotone, drawn on twos.
summary: Albretsen AS is presented as an animation studio where every product is a painted cel and the company mark is a 3D object you can grab and throw. The ancestry of motion (Muybridge, Marey, the 1840 phenakistiscope) is recut in two inks and lives on the page as real imagery, so the craft shows instead of being claimed. It reads as a small studio with feature-length ambition: precise, playful and very deliberate.
voice: Studio-floor shorthand from someone who ships: short, concrete, a little cinematic, never salesy. Example: "Four products on the stand right now. Drag them to re-cut the order."
motion: Characters move on twos (12 drawings a second) with smears, squash and impact frames, while scroll and camera stay smooth; nothing ever blurs.
sound: Off until switched on; then synthesised cel thwacks on impacts and a pencil tick on every edit, no audio files.
mark: An extruded cel-shaded A with a hard ink line and a two-tone toon shader, the same geometry as a flat SVG mark and a live three.js object you can throw.

name: Same Room
tagline: One voxel room, 2019 and today, with a time scrubber as the split edge
summary: The hero is a single isometric voxel room rendered twice from the same camera: the bedroom desk where Fun Libs was built at 17 and the studio it became. Dragging the edge between them scrubs through real milestones from 2016 to 2026, shedding pastel blocks as it moves. It reads as an optimistic builder who keeps placing the next block, and the craft (code-baked voxels, a CSS-3D shelf with the real product logos, spring physics everywhere) carries the skill without saying so.
voice: Plain, sunny and concrete: say what got built and what it did, then stop. Example: "Same room. Bigger builds."
motion: Everything is a block that is either placed or about to be: springs that land with a small overshoot (Stack Drop), an edge that follows on a spring and sheds voxels (Edge Drift), and pills that lean toward the cursor (Magnetic Pull).
sound: Off by default; when switched on, a short wooden block click whose pitch rises with each year the seam passes, and a soft tick when a shelf cube lifts.
mark: A 2×2×2 butter block with its front corner missing and a leaf-green block dropping into the gap, beside a pixel wordmark with a butter voxel extrusion.

name: The Albretsen Dawn
tagline: A morning paper from the future, printed by a press that only knows triangles.
summary: The homepage is the front page of a newspaper from about 2036, set in pastel low-poly light. A canvas press prints the lead plate live from the sun outward. A three.js crystal of the mark breaks out of the photograph, and a real wire of product events runs down the rail. The newspaper is only the frame. Everything printed inside it is plainly made by software, so a small technology company reads as calm, exact and quietly ambitious.
voice: Quiet confidence: headlines are facts, never adjectives, with lots of air around them. Example: "A word game built at 17 now has 113,000+ installs."
motion: Things print, not pop: facets arrive from the sun outward, pages turn on a diagonal facet (View Transitions API), and nothing bounces.
sound: Off until the visitor turns it on, then a soft synthesised paper tick on edition turns, copies and theme changes.
mark: A faceted A built from eleven triangles lit from the upper right, with a warm sunrise triangle in the crossbar and a gold four-point spark off the apex; in 3D it becomes the crystal.

name: Darkfield
tagline: One glass slide you pan and zoom, with every product lit from the side.
summary: Darkfield microscopy lights only what is really there, so the specimen glows on black. The homepage is a glass slide you can pan and zoom. Albretsen AS products are arranged around a stone of 24,000 grains, like a Victorian diatom slide. Wherever the objective settles, the grains fly over and become that product's specimen glyph. It shows taste and engineering in the same gesture, and every number on it is true.
voice: Quiet, exact and slightly scientific: it names what something is and what it measures, then stops. Example: "Builds software that pays for itself. Everything he has shipped is on this slide."
motion: Like an objective finding focus: things arrive out of blur with an expo-out ease, the slide moves slowly between places, and the grains converge, ripple on a live signal and peel away as you scroll.
sound: Off by default. Once it is on, a soft two-partial sine ping marks a signal, a change of focus or a live event from the product under the objective.
mark: A triangular Triceratium diatom valve that reads as an A, with three ocelli and one signal-gold nodule, beside an outlined Instrument Serif wordmark.

name: Drift
tagline: A river of time in soft plastic, from a first Android app in 2016 to today.
summary: The homepage opens on a live three.js river: nine thousand glossy beads carry ten years of work toward the viewer, and the visitor can drag a pebble through the years or stir the water. Every surface is one hue (OKLCH 180) in twelve depths and lit like a studio product shot. That calm precision is what Albretsen AS should signal: someone who ships often, keeps what works and lets the rest settle.
voice: Calm, exact and unhurried. It describes what exists and lets the numbers stay small. Example: "Ten years downstream of a first Android app."
motion: One hand-rolled spring drives everything, from the river's stir to the popovers, so nothing moves on a timeline and everything drifts, overshoots a little and settles.
sound: Off by default. When turned on, synthesised water droplets mark ripples, year changes and live events, and a falling or rising four-note chord plays when the tide turns.
mark: A single-storey 'a' whose bowl is a bead and whose stem flows out into a current, with one small bead floating free.

name: Say Cheese
tagline: A loud candy-clay camera world where the visitor holds the camera: pull focus, set exposure, keep the print.
summary: Albretsen AS through a viewfinder. Blink, a squishy butter-yellow clay camera rendered live by a hand-written WebGL2 raymarcher, stands in for the company: hand-made warmth on top of serious engineering. The hero hands the visitor the controls (lens ring, exposure, shutter) and every print they take carries a real fact, so the skill shows itself instead of being claimed.
voice: Sunny, blunt and proud, with camera words doing the work. Example: "Four things, developing."
motion: Everything moves like a camera handled by a person: the iris opens, focus hunts once and locks, the shutter flashes, clay squashes and springs back (Web Animations API, springs baked into linear()).
sound: Off until asked; then every sound is synthesised live: a soft plastic shutter, the autofocus double-beep, ring detent ticks, a clay squish and a sticker slap.
mark: Blink's face: a butter clay pebble with a bubblegum lens ring whose three-blade aperture forms the letter A, next to a wordmark rolled from clay coils.

name: Stille
tagline: A quiet archive of working things: an app store, art-directed by a museum.
summary: The products sit on one long white shelf in Hammershøi daylight, photographed like objects in a museum store: real icons as glazed tiles, retired products as plaster casts, one violet cube. Everything can be picked up and rearranged, and every object opens into its catalogue card. It reads as quiet confidence: few things, all of them made to work.
voice: Short, plain, unhurried; says less than it could. Example: "Arrange them in any order. Nothing is saved. It is only a shelf."
motion: Objects move like things set down by hand: View Transitions glide the shelf into its new order, the dropped object kicks and settles, and a tile opens into its catalogue plate while the room drops to grey.
sound: Off until asked; then one synthesised knock of a ceramic tile on a painted board when something is set down, and nothing else.
mark: An A drawn as a house gable with a shelf across it and one aniline-violet square resting on the shelf; the wordmark is Instrument Serif in outline with AS in Geist Mono.

name: Nocturne Select
tagline: A character-select screen where the products are the characters, in glossy plastic lit like a studio at night.
summary: The homepage is a select screen: four live products stand on lit plinths in a real-time three.js stage, a stat sheet locks onto whichever one you pick, and its live wire shows what that product is doing right now. Everything is soft plastic rendered in code under one magenta and one ion rim light, with Met Open Access objects giving it a lineage. It reads as a builder with range and finish: many products, each owned, each lit properly.
voice: Short, calm, exact; a stat sheet more than a pitch. "Four on stage. Seven kept in resin."
motion: Things power on from a scan line, lock in with a soft plastic overshoot, rise off the floor as you scroll, and otherwise breathe slowly in the dark.
sound: Off by default; once turned on, each selection plays a two-note sine and triangle lock through a lowpass, like a soft plastic click.
mark: The Selector: a rounded Λ that is both the A of Albretsen and the P1 pointer, with an ion dot for the one chosen; it doubles as the cursor and the 3D pointer above the selected product.

name: Habit
tagline: A quiet conversation at a pen-drawn desk, with a crystal you can turn.
summary: The site talks to the visitor in short, typed turns from an ink drawing of a desk, and answers in its own voice: chips, free text, and a mode that turns the products into plain specs for agents. Real 3D (Kenney models and generated crystal habits) is drawn by three.js as ink, after James Sowerby's British Mineralogy plates, and the only colour on the page comes from 200-year-old hand-coloured specimens and the real product logos. It reads as someone effective and unhurried who builds technical things with taste.
voice: Short, factual, a little dry; the site speaks in turns with a typing beat before each one. Example: "Habit is a mineralogist's word: the shape a crystal keeps growing into."
motion: Ink draws itself in, bubbles unfold from their tails after a typing beat, and the theme switches through a wobbly hand-drawn circle grown from the lamp bulb; nothing moves more than about 18 px.
sound: Off by default; once enabled, each turn lands with two soft pencil ticks synthesised from band-passed noise.
mark: An octahedron drawn Sowerby-style, front edges in ink and back edges dashed, whose top half reads as an A, beside an Instrument Serif wordmark set in outlines.

name: IR//PEEL
tagline: Pixel stickers on glossy vinyl. Peel one and an infrared underdrawing is underneath.
summary: The homepage is a sheet of die-cut vinyl stickers: the Albretsen AS mark, the four real product logos and a set of pixel sprites. Visitors can peel every one of them. Under each sticker is a fact, and under the mark is an infrared, Bayer-dithered plate of a public-domain museum object. The surface is playful, but there is always a deliberate layer under it, which suits a builder who ships toys and infrastructure with the same care.
voice: Terse and dry, the way a late-night terminal talks. Lowercase confidence that never shouts. Example: "Every sticker on this sheet peels. Underneath is the work."
motion: Objects behave like vinyl: they SLAP down on a spring, LIFT with a holographic glint, peel along a real fold line, and screens dissolve in Bayer-ordered infrared.
sound: Off until the visitor turns it on. Then a band-passed noise sweep plays when vinyl lifts off the liner, there is a low thump on re-stick, and 8-bit square-wave blips on UI.
mark: A 16×16 pixel tile in violet with its corner folded back and an A carrying a one-pixel magenta offset, set beside a pixel wordmark with an orange AS.

name: Sodium Orbit
tagline: Earth at night from the ISS: a playable spark lights four lamps, and the lamps light the introduction.
summary: Seen from orbit, cities at night are sodium-orange circuit boards under a thin blue airglow. The hero is a small game on a real NASA photograph: fly a molten spark through four cold lamps, one per product, and each lamp strikes neon pink, warms to sodium and lights one part of the sentence 'Asgeir Albretsen builds software that pays for itself.' It shows craft by doing rather than claiming, and keeps every figure real.
voice: Calm, exact, a little dry; facts in place of adjectives. Example: 'Four lamps on. A few burned out on the way.'
motion: Everything arrives the way a sodium lamp strikes: a neon flicker, then a slow warm-up to orange, then rest, all written with the Web Animations API and spring easings sampled into linear().
sound: Off until asked for; then each lamp strikes with a synthesised starter click, a flickering neon buzz and a warm hum, and the live feed ticks quietly.
mark: The arc of a thrown spark forms an A, with the glowing spark itself as the crossbar; the game's lamps sit on that arc and finishing the game draws it in particles.

name: Violet Cabinet
tagline: A museum archive plugged into the mains: five electrified plates, one crystal that changes habit, a bust digitised live.
summary: Albretsen AS is shown as a cabinet of working software. Real public-domain scans (Kurr's 1859 crystal plates, West's Franklin, Tesla's 1899 lab, Haeckel) are electrified violet, and the homepage is a scroll-driven story in plates: the SVG specimen morphs from cube to octahedron to quartz to dodecahedron and finally into the twin-crystal mark while a CC0 marble bust is scanned into a live engraving. The precision is real (84°33′ Japan-law twin, Plate A habits, catalogue numbering) and the play is in the motion, which suits a builder who is both rigorous and quick.
voice: A catalogue entry written by someone with a sense of humour: exact, short, numbered, never selling. Example: "Built at seventeen. No marketing, ever. Version 5 shipped in 2026."
motion: Scroll turns the plates: CSS view timelines on scene spacers cut each new scan open from a hexagonal crystal section around its focal point, while Lenis smooths the scroll and one spark discharges between plates.
sound: Off until asked; when on, each plate change gives a short band-passed electrical crackle over a faint 50 Hz hum.
mark: Two quartz crystals joined at exactly 84°33′ (a Japan-law twin) form an A, with a spark-yellow bar as the crossbar current; the scroll morph ends on it.

name: Halflight
tagline: A title sequence that resolves into a page, printed in two inks and lit by the real sun over Oslo.
summary: The site opens like a film: shutters, a spark on a NASA horizon, a halftone field pulling focus into a photograph, then the name. Every surface after that is a two-ink duotone whose inks follow the actual solar altitude over Oslo, and visitors can drag the sun across today's sky to re-light the whole page. It reads as one person with cinematic ambition and the patience to get every frame right, which is what Albretsen AS sells.
voice: Title-card brevity, credits-roll calm: facts set like a film's opening credits, never a sales line. Example: "Software that pays for itself. Apps, SaaS and agent infrastructure, written and shipped from 59° north."
motion: Reveals sharpen rather than fade: everything moves from coarse to fine, over-exposed to printed, on long filmic ease-outs, and the letterbox only ever opens.
sound: Off until asked; then a soft three-voice drone tuned to the phase of day whose filter opens as the sun climbs, with a single 1.3 kHz glint when you grab the sun.
mark: A solid half-sun on the horizon over a tapering halftone reflection; it rises, prints its reflection dot by dot, then breathes (Lottie), beside an outlined Instrument Serif wordmark with a Geist Mono AS.

name: The Vivarium
tagline: Small software, kept alive under glass.
summary: Albretsen AS presented as a tended terrarium: each product is a small creature living under a CSS-3D glass case, catalogued like a naturalist would, with real 17th and 18th century specimen drawings from The Met pinned beside storybook three.js creatures. The tension between the still archive and the living jar shows both taste and technical skill, and retired products stay visible as pressed herbarium sheets, which reads as honest and long-term.
type: Fraunces (opsz 144, SOFT 50; italic SOFT 100 for Latin names)
voice: A calm naturalist's field notes: exact, a little dry, never selling. Example: "Four creatures live in the case. Seven are pressed and filed."
motion: Everything grows rather than slides: bottom-anchored germinate reveals, a glass case that lands with a soft overshoot and turns under your hand with inertia, and idle life only in short bursts.
sound: Off by default; when switched on, tapping a creature rings a small glass tink tuned per species and turning a herbarium sheet makes a soft paper rustle (Web Audio, no files).
mark: A bell jar over a two-leaf sprout with the right leaf in moss, paired with an outlined Fraunces wordmark, a moss full stop and a mono AS.

name: Plate Nocturne
tagline: A light table at night: 19th-century glass negatives under loose panes that bend the light.
summary: The homepage is a light table. Loose panes of glass lie over glass-negative photographs from The Met's open-access collection: Moussette's 1886 lightning, an 1883 eclipse corona, Whipple's moon, and Paul Henry's Cygnus and Lyra. Each pane displaces what is under it, the way the Albretsen mark bends its ray. The people who made those plates did it after their day's work with instruments they built themselves, which is the honest story of Albretsen AS: one person who builds at night and keeps what pays for itself.
voice: The quiet operator: short, exact, unhurried, with numbers given and never inflated. Labels read like museum catalogue entries. Example: "Software, developed after dark."
motion: Light develops instead of animating: photographs resolve from over-exposed amber haze to sharp, panes stack and recede on scroll, and plate changes open from a single seam of amber light.
sound: Off until asked. Everything is synthesised in Web Audio: a struck-glass tink, a spark crackle when the bolt fires, a pane sliding, and a low hum while sound is on.
mark: An A made of two glass plates seen edge-on, leaning together, with one amber ray that kinks as it passes through each plate. The ray draws itself on load.

name: Honest Pixels
tagline: Real photographs, rounded down by code, captioned with exactly what was done to them.
summary: Every image is a CC0 photograph run through Asgeir's own dither, ASCII and engraving code, and every image says so. The hero is a moodboard you can rearrange and re-render live (Photo, Dither, ASCII), and it doubles as the portfolio: each piece is a product, a fact or a process. The same honesty runs through the numbers: two live, one building, one paused, seven retired, all listed.
voice: Plain, exact and unflattering about itself; it states the source and the number. Example: "I build software that pays for itself. Some of it didn't. This site says which."
motion: Things move in steps, like pixels do (Bayer-ordered reveals, stepped counters, 1 Hz cursor); easing is allowed only where a hand is dragging.
sound: Off until asked; then 1-bit square-wave blips with hard envelopes for pick-up, drop, render switch and each scroll step of the develop band.
mark: A pixel 'A' that dithers away toward the top beside a blinking brass cursor block, next to 'albretsen' in outlined Bricolage and 'AS' in Plex Mono.

name: Escape Vector
tagline: Public-domain spaceflight pushed to hard black and white, with one re-entry red for everything alive.
summary: A self-funded builder who left orbit on purpose. The hero is a landing site: a crater field built from twenty CSS 3D contour slices, where a red probe reads altitude under the cursor and locks onto real product beacons standing on the high ground. NASA photography, Trouvelot engravings and Haeckel's radiolarians make it feel like a real archive, and decode-into-place type and spring physics make it feel engineered.
voice: Precise, a little defiant, never corporate. Short declaratives with physics in them. Example: "Four up. Seven came down."
motion: Everything has mass: hand-rolled damped springs for tilt, lift and float, and text that arrives as noise and locks in left to right.
sound: Off until asked; then tiny sine blips on probe locks, decoded figures and new downlink events, pitched down like telemetry.
mark: A vector capital A whose tip has come loose and floats, tilted 10 degrees in burn red; the tip launches on hover.

name: Specimen Drop
tagline: A product-drop page for a whole company: every product is a crystal on a live lapis geode.
summary: Albretsen AS is presented as a naturalist's cabinet released like a product drop. Public-domain botanical and natural-history plates are re-inked in ultramarine, which was once ground from lapis lazuli. The hero is a live three.js geode: each crystal is a product you can pull off and re-seat, and a museum label hangs beside it on a spring. It reads as skilled, warm and careful, and it is clearly technology, because the specimens are software and the cabinet runs live.
voice: A careful collector in the first person: warm, specific and unhurried, and never selling. Example: "Software, grown & mounted."
motion: Every movement uses one hand-rolled damped spring: crystals drop and re-seat, stickers dangle while carried, the label swings like a pendulum, and cards settle onto the page.
sound: Off until the visitor turns it on. After that, synthesised glass tinks play when a crystal re-seats or the label is let go, and a soft paper rustle plays when a card is laid down.
mark: A cut-stone A with bevelled facets lit from the upper left, beside a Fraunces wordmark outlined to paths with an italic AS.

name: Cover Story
tagline: The current issue of a magazine about one company, with stickers you can peel off and slap anywhere.
summary: The homepage is a magazine cover you can open: a three.js cover that bends on its spine, a real magnifying glass that magnifies its print, and a glass crystal rising from the inside spread, which turns the story column into a contents page. Editorial serif and NASA crystal photography carry the gravitas; neo-brutalist stickers carry every fact from content.js, and visitors can peel them off a sticker sheet and put them on the page themselves. It reads as someone with taste and range who ships, never as a bank or a consultancy.
voice: Editorial and dry, an amused magazine writing about a serious subject. Example: "Small products, shipped, then left to compound."
motion: Stickers slap down with an overshoot and their hard shadows land a beat later, while paper turns slowly on its spine. Everything else holds still.
sound: Off by default. When it is on, the sounds are made from filtered noise: a short thump when a sticker lands, a bright swish when one peels off, and a breath of air when the cover turns.
mark: A violet sticker with an Archivo 'A' whose corner peels back to a lime underside, the same gesture as opening the cover.

name: Pocket Planet
tagline: A pocket-sized voxel world that never stops working, and a cursor that keeps prying it apart.
summary: Albretsen AS drawn as a tiny isometric planet: every glowing tower is something shipped, and live activity from the products is launched off its surface into a physics pile you can grab and throw. Careful construction with one deliberate block out of place reads as a builder who is exact, quick and slightly mischievous, which is the person behind a one-company product line.
voice: Dry, exact and a little cheeky; states what was built and lets the numbers sit there. Example: "You knocked the full stop off. It will find its way back."
motion: Things are flung, never faded: spring overshoot on entrances, real gravity on live events, and a view transition that swallows the page into the pointer.
sound: Off until asked; then soft synthesised ticks when blocks land, a two-note chirp on copy, and a low swoop when the planet is rerolled.
mark: A 3x3x3 isometric voxel cube whose near-corner block has been launched out of its slot, with speed lines; the block springs out on hover.
